questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was very interested in going on Exchange a place with rich nature and opportunities around it. Hiking, swimming, going on trips etc. Also, the reputation of the University of Bergen was very good and the courses in the catalogue sounded like a match for my field of study. It was also an important aspect for me to go to a smaller city, because I think it is easier to be integrated and feel somewhat like a local, when the place is smaller.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was allright if you searched for it, but I think it was confusing that the different deadlines and important informations were spread on many different digital platforms.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a detailed study/course introduction and were presented to the person responsible for the faculty of science.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was allright, but I spend many hours searching for a place on
Hybel.no
. I found something by luck only 14 days before, but it was a hustle the time before. But
Hybel.no
and luck was crucial for my finding of housing!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That you need to start searching for it as soon as possible, but that it is really cozy and a good way of creating a community on your own.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Through university partnership

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was through the university partnership, and the registration proces was good

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The studentcenter and the person in responsbility of the faculty.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was overall pretty succesful, because I found open courses. I think it was tougher for the restricted courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reach for help if you doubt anything about the proces

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of the courses were easier than it is at my home university. I had expected a higher burden of both classes you needed to attend and reading. It was nice with a lot of freetime, but I could have wished for more classes to attend.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Less hours to attend, and the seminar classes were lead by other students in the host institution, which is the most important differences.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Cities
Climate Policy
Current Anthropological Research: The Class on Class: Towards an Anthropology of Capitalism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can really recommend Current Anthropological Research: The Class on Class: Towards an Anthropology of Capitalism, because it was mostly analogue and the teacher was very interesting and dedicated.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Transportation and high prices in the supermarket

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Alcohol was more expected in Bergen, cigarettes, some food-entities were more expensive, others were more cheap.
Clothes were for me cheaper in Bergen than in CPH

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think Uib is very good at promoting both activities, sports, bars, musical and cultural events and it seems like there is also much freedom for the students to engage in or create new projects or clubs, if the wish. Well done

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend getting a part of a sports club, where the community seems to be nice. 
I would also recommend spending time at the different studentbars and to go different events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend going to DNT-cabins in Norway. 
Go on hikes and use all the different facilities at Sammen.
Go out to get a beer, go to cultural events (cinema, museums and book store Litteraturhuset)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was allright, since DK and Norway is not that far apart culturally.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend events, reach out to people and try to join some sort of club or organization.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not that many, maybe the club life was kind of heavy and less chill to go grab a beer.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Nature, the sweet people, all the events that the university of Bergen has hosted and promoted for us. It is very appreciated.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy the nature!!
Reach out to people you like
Attend organizations
Try to rest in your choices and prioritize where to spend your energy

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont think so

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: More peace, new routines, sports, hiking, a new way of living, that I really appreciated.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Reaching out to people and making new everyday life for yourself, especially when I didn't have much classes to attend.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It has been a very good experience in all, I recommend Bergen so much! Remember rainjacket!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
